literal: Jiong's general Xi Piluo, with a host of a hundred thousand, camped at Pei County intending to attack Xu Province.
idiomatic: Jiong's general Xi Piluo camped at Pei with a hundred thousand men, set to strike Xu.

literal: His wife and children were at Jinxiang.
idiomatic: His family was at Jinxiang.

literal: Zhongwen sent a man falsely posing as Piluo's envoy to say to Xu Shanjing, lord of Jinxiang: "Tan Rang will reach Jinxiang tomorrow at noon to proclaim the Duke of Shu's order and reward the officers."
idiomatic: Zhongwen sent a false envoy to Jinxiang's lord Xu Shanjing: "Tan Rang arrives tomorrow at noon to proclaim the Duke of Shu's order and reward the troops."

literal: The people of Jinxiang thought it true and were all pleased.
idiomatic: Jinxiang believed it and rejoiced.

literal: Zhongwen picked elite troops and falsely raised Jiong's banners and flags.
idiomatic: Zhongwen picked elite troops and flew Jiong's banners falsely.

literal: Shanjing thought Tan Rang had arrived and went out of the city to meet and pay respects.
idiomatic: Shanjing thought Tan Rang had come and went out to welcome him.

literal: Zhongwen seized him and then took Jinxiang.
idiomatic: Zhongwen seized him and took Jinxiang.

literal: The generals urged slaughter; Zhongwen said: "We should treat their wives and children leniently and their soldiers will return of themselves."
idiomatic: The generals urged massacre; Zhongwen said, "Spare their families and the soldiers will come over."

literal: "If we slaughter at once, they will all be cut off."
idiomatic: "Slaughter them now and every man will fight to the death."

literal: The masses all praised it as good.
idiomatic: All approved.

literal: Thereupon Piluo, relying on his numbers, came to press the government army; Zhongwen with his back to the city formed ranks and set ambush; when the troops moved, all together pulled brushwood drums and raised a clamor.
idiomatic: Piluo, trusting his numbers, pressed the government army; Zhongwen formed with his back to the wall, set ambush, and at the signal every man dragged brushwood drums and roared.

literal: Piluo's army collapsed; all threw themselves into the Zhu River and died, and the water did not flow.
idiomatic: Piluo's army broke; men threw themselves into the Zhu until the river would not flow.

literal: Tan Rang was captured and sent to the capital in a caged cart; Henan was entirely pacified.
idiomatic: Tan Rang was taken in a cage cart to the capital; Henan was pacified.

literal: Piluo hid in a house in Xingyang; seized and beheaded, his head was sent to the palace gate.
idiomatic: Piluo hid in Xingyang; seized and beheaded, his head was sent to the capital.

literal: A stone was carved to record the merit and set up on the Si.
idiomatic: A stone was carved to record the victory and set up on the Si.

literal: He entered court at the capital; Emperor Wen led him into the inner chamber and their feast was exceedingly merry.
idiomatic: He came to court; Emperor Wen brought him to the inner chamber and feasted him in great joy.

literal: He was granted a thousand bolts of mixed colored silk, ten singing girls, and appointed Pillar of State.
idiomatic: He was given a thousand bolts of silk, ten singing girls, and made Pillar of State.

literal: Just then Emperor Wen received the abdication and did not go.
idiomatic: Just then Wen received the abdication and Zhongwen did not attend.

literal: Before long his uncle the Grand Commandant Yi was imprisoned for an offense; Zhongwen was also audited by the clerks, and in prison he submitted a memorial saying: "Formerly when Yuchi Jiong rebelled, everywhere men followed the scene."
idiomatic: Soon his uncle Grand Commandant Yi was jailed; Zhongwen was audited too and from prison wrote: "When Yuchi Jiong rebelled, men followed him everywhere."

literal: "I held a post at the passes and rivers in a place of strategic weight; I once rinsed my girdle and slept with my spear, vowing certain death."
idiomatic: "I held the passes in a vital post, rinsed my belt and slept with my spear, sworn to die."

literal: "At the time Jiong offered to buy me with the rank of Great General and a fief of ten thousand households."
idiomatic: "Jiong offered me Great General and ten thousand households."

literal: "I did not regard wife and children and did not cherish my life."
idiomatic: "I gave up wife and children and my own life."

literal: "I braved bare blades, broke heavy encirclements; three sons and one daughter perished in succession."
idiomatic: "I broke through steel; three sons and a daughter fell one after another."

literal: "I laid bare liver and gall and raced to the palace gate."
idiomatic: "I laid bare my heart and came to the throne."

literal: "I received from Your Majesty high office and was entrusted with arms."
idiomatic: "Your Majesty gave me high rank and an army."

literal: "At that time Henan's fierce bandits glared like wolves and spread like owls."
idiomatic: "Henan's rebels glared like wolves and spread like kites."

literal: "With eight thousand worn troops I swept away the miasma."
idiomatic: "With eight thousand worn men I swept the miasma away."

literal: "I overthrew Liu Xiaokuan at Liang Commandery and broke Tan Rang at Liaodi;"
idiomatic: "I broke Liu Xiaokuan at Liang and Tan Rang at Liaodi;"

literal: "pacified Cao, recovered Dong, secured Chengwu, settled Yongchang;"
idiomatic: "pacified Cao, recovered Dong, held Chengwu, settled Yongchang;"

literal: "relieved Bozhou's siege and defeated the Xu bandits."
idiomatic: "lifted Bozhou's siege and beat Xu;"

literal: "Xi Piluo's host of a hundred thousand collapsed in one battle."
idiomatic: "Piluo's hundred thousand fell in one fight."

literal: "Henan's swarming rebels were pacified at the proper time."
idiomatic: "Henan's swarms were cut down in season."

literal: "When the many villains contended for the tripod and living creatures lacked a master, my second uncle Yi was first at You Province, commanding Yan and Zhao."
idiomatic: "When traitors fought for the realm and the people had no lord, my second uncle Yi held You, commanding Yan and Zhao."

literal: "South he neighbored many bandits; north he swept the barbarian banners; within he pacified, without he soothed, and escaped guilt."
idiomatic: "South he faced rebels, north he swept the frontier, within and without he kept the peace and stood clear."

literal: "My fifth uncle Zhi raised the standard at Heishui, neighbored Wang Qian, checked the barbarian valleys, and pacified the Shu road."
idiomatic: "My fifth uncle Zhi raised the standard at Heishui beside Wang Qian, checked the barbarian passes, and held the Shu road."

literal: "My elder brother Yan governed Huainan, sat and controlled fierce enemies, seized the moment to pacify them, and sent heads to the capital."
idiomatic: "My brother Yan held Huainan, pinned fierce foes, struck when he could, and sent heads to the capital."

literal: "Wang Qian secretly held two provinces and rebelled across the three Shu."
idiomatic: "Wang Qian held two provinces and rebelled across Shu."

literal: "My third uncle Yi received the war-meat in the temple court and reverently executed Heaven's punishment."
idiomatic: "My third uncle Yi took the temple charge and carried out Heaven's punishment."

literal: "Besides these, father, uncles, and brothers all bore heavy civil and military trust."
idiomatic: "Beyond them, father, uncles, and brothers all bore heavy trust of court and camp."

literal: "Some received orders in peril; some attended the hook formation as guards—the whole house sincere, hoping there is what can be made clear."
idiomatic: "Some took orders in peril, some guarded the throne—the whole house loyal, and something may yet be shown."

literal: "I humbly wish you to grant the grace of tears for the guiltless and send down rain and cloud favor, then cold ash will blaze again and withered bone return to flesh."
idiomatic: "Grant tears for the guiltless and rain from heaven, and cold ash will live and dry bone grow flesh again."

literal: The emperor read the memorial and released both Yi and Zhongwen.
idiomatic: The emperor read it and freed both Yi and Zhongwen.

literal: The next year he was appointed Campaign Commander-in-Chief, commanding twelve provincial commanders to strike the Hu.
idiomatic: Next year he was Campaign Commander-in-Chief over twelve provinces against the Hu.

literal: He went out to Fuyuan garrison, met the barbarians, and defeated them.
idiomatic: At Fuyuan he met the barbarians and beat them.

literal: Thereupon from the Golden River he went out by White Road.
idiomatic: Then from the Golden River he marched by White Road.

literal: He sent the commanders Xin Mingjin, Yuan Pang, Helan Zhi, Lü Chu, Duan Xie, and others with twenty thousand men out by the Shengle route toward Napie Mountain.
idiomatic: He sent Xin Mingjin, Yuan Pang, Helan Zhi, Lü Chu, Duan Xie, and others with twenty thousand by the Shengle road toward Napie Mountain.

literal: North of Protecting-the-Army Province they met the barbarians.
idiomatic: North of Protecting-the-Army they met the enemy.

literal: The khan saw Zhongwen's army array neat and stern and withdrew without fighting.
idiomatic: The khan saw Zhongwen's ranks trim and stern and withdrew without battle.

literal: Zhongwen crossed the mountains in pursuit.
idiomatic: Zhongwen crossed the mountains in pursuit.

literal: On his return, because the documents of the Masters of Writing were complex and clerks were much given to fraud, the emperor ordered Zhongwen to examine and record affairs within the ministry; what he exposed and impeached was very many.
idiomatic: On his return, finding the Masters of Writing's records tangled and clerks corrupt, the emperor had Zhongwen audit the ministry; he exposed many.

literal: The emperor praised his clear judgment and richly rewarded and comforted him.
idiomatic: The emperor praised his clarity and rewarded him richly.

literal: The emperor often worried that transport could not be supplied; Zhongwen asked to cut the Wei and open a canal.
idiomatic: The emperor often worried over supply; Zhongwen proposed cutting the Wei and opening a canal.

literal: The emperor approved it and had Zhongwen oversee the matter.
idiomatic: The emperor agreed and put Zhongwen in charge.

literal: In the campaign against Chen he was appointed Campaign Commander-in-Chief.
idiomatic: In the campaign against Chen he was Campaign Commander-in-Chief.

literal: When Gao Zhihui and others rebelled in Jiangnan, Zhongwen was again Campaign Commander-in-Chief to suppress them.
idiomatic: When Gao Zhihui rebelled in the south, Zhongwen again commanded the campaign.

literal: At the time the three armies lacked food and rice and grain soared in price; Zhongwen privately sold army grain and was dismissed from his name.
idiomatic: The armies starved and grain soared; Zhongwen sold army grain privately and was struck from the rolls.

literal: The next year his office and rank were restored and he led troops to garrison Mayi against the Hu.
idiomatic: Next year his rank was restored and he garrisoned Mayi against the Hu.

literal: Prince of Jin Guang, because Zhongwen had talent as a commander, always kept him in mind; at this he memorialized him, and he was then ordered to supervise the Prince of Jin's military headquarters.
idiomatic: Prince Guang valued his generalship and now recommended him; he was ordered to supervise the prince's headquarters.

literal: Later when the Turks raided the frontier, the Prince of Jin was supreme commander and sent Zhongwen to lead the vanguard; he greatly defeated the bandits and returned.
idiomatic: When Turks raided the border, Prince Guang was supreme commander and sent Zhongwen with the vanguard; he routed them and returned.

literal: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, Zhongwen was transferred to Grand General of the Left Wing Guard and took part in selecting civil and military appointments.
idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Zhongwen became Grand General of the Left Wing Guard and helped choose civil and military men.

literal: He followed the emperor in the campaign against Tuyuhun and was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Brightness, greatly favored and trusted.
idiomatic: He followed the emperor against Tuyuhun, was made Grand Master of Splendid Brightness, and was deeply trusted.

literal: In the Liaodong campaign Zhongwen led the army on the Lelang route.
idiomatic: In the Liaodong war he led the Lelang column.

literal: When they halted at Wugu City, Zhongwen chose several thousand lean horses and donkeys and placed them at the rear of the army; then he led the host eastward past.
idiomatic: At Wugu he placed several thousand lean horses and donkeys at the rear, then marched east.

literal: Goryeo sent troops to mask and strike the baggage train; Zhongwen turned back and struck, greatly defeating them.
idiomatic: Goryeo struck the baggage train; he turned and broke them.

literal: When they reached the Yalu, the Goryeo general Yi Zhizhi Wen De feigned surrender and came into his camp.
idiomatic: At the Yalu, Goryeo's Yi Zhizhi Wen De feigned surrender and entered his camp.

literal: Zhongwen had earlier received a secret order that if he met Gao Yuan and Wen De he must capture them.
idiomatic: He had a secret order to seize Gao Yuan and Wen De if he met them.

literal: At this Wen De came; Zhongwen was about to seize him.
idiomatic: Wen De came; Zhongwen was about to seize him.

literal: At the time the Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Shilong was comfort-and-soothe commissioner and firmly stopped it.
idiomatic: Right Vice Director Liu Shilong, the soothe commissioner, firmly stopped him.

literal: Zhongwen then released Wen De.
idiomatic: Zhongwen let Wen De go.

literal: Shortly he regretted it and sent a man to deceive Wen De saying: "There is further to discuss—you may come again."
idiomatic: Soon he regretted it and sent word: "There is more to discuss—come again."

literal: Wen De would not comply and crossed the river.
idiomatic: Wen De refused and crossed the river.

literal: Zhongwen chose cavalry to cross the water in pursuit; in each battle he defeated the bandits.
idiomatic: Zhongwen crossed with cavalry and beat them in every fight.

literal: Wen De sent Zhongwen a poem saying: "Divine stratagems probe Heaven's patterns, subtle reckoning exhausts Earth's principles."
idiomatic: Wen De sent a poem: "Divine stratagems probe heaven, subtle reckoning exhausts earth."

literal: "Victory's merit is already high; to know sufficiency is the wish to rest on clouds."
idiomatic: "Your victory is high; knowing enough, rest upon the clouds."

literal: Zhongwen answered with a letter instructing him; Wen De burned his palisade and fled.
idiomatic: Zhongwen answered instructing him; Wen De burned his camp and fled.

literal: At the time Yuwen Shu, because grain was exhausted, wished to return; Zhongwen argued that with elite troops pursuing Wen De there could be achievement.
idiomatic: Yuwen Shu, grain gone, wished to retreat; Zhongwen argued elite pursuit of Wen De could win.

literal: Shu firmly stopped him; Zhongwen angrily said: "The general commands a host of a hundred thousand yet cannot break a small bandit—with what face will you see the emperor?"
idiomatic: Shu refused; Zhongwen snapped, "You lead a hundred thousand and cannot crush this flea—what face will you show the emperor?"

literal: "Moreover this journey of Zhongwen's is certainly without achievement!"
idiomatic: "And this campaign of mine is already ruined!"

literal: Shu therefore said in a harsh voice: "How do you know there is no achievement?"
idiomatic: Shu barked, "How do you know there is none?"

literal: Zhongwen said: "In former days when Zhou Yafu was general, he met the Son of Heaven and the army's bearing did not change."
idiomatic: Zhongwen said, "When Zhou Yafu commanded, he met the Son of Heaven and the army's bearing never shifted."

literal: "The outcome rested on one man—therefore merit was established and the name completed."
idiomatic: "Victory hung on one will—therefore fame was made."

literal: "Now each man has his own heart—how can one go to meet the enemy?"
idiomatic: "Now every man has his own heart—how can we fight?"

literal: At the beginning the emperor, because Zhongwen had plans, had ordered the armies to consult and follow his command—therefore there was this speech.
idiomatic: The emperor had given Zhongwen command over the armies—hence these words.

literal: Because of this Shu and the rest had no choice but to follow.
idiomatic: Shu and the rest had no choice but to follow.

literal: They then marched and eastward reached Sa Water.
idiomatic: They marched east to Sa Water.

literal: Yuwen Shu because the troops were hungry withdrew and returned; the army then suffered great defeat.
idiomatic: Yuwen Shu retreated for hunger; the army was ruined.

literal: The emperor handed them to the law officers; the generals all shifted blame onto Zhongwen.
idiomatic: The emperor handed them to the law; every general blamed Zhongwen.

literal: The emperor was greatly angry, released the generals, and alone imprisoned Zhongwen.
idiomatic: The emperor raged, freed the generals, and jailed Zhongwen alone.

literal: Zhongwen, worried and resentful, fell ill; when critically ill he was released.
idiomatic: Zhongwen, sick with grief, grew desperate; only then was he released.

literal: He died at home, aged sixty-eight.
idiomatic: He died at home, aged sixty-eight.

literal: He compiled Abridgment of the Han Dynastic Histories in thirty scrolls and Overview in thirty scrolls.
idiomatic: He wrote Abridgment of the Han Histories in thirty scrolls and Overview in thirty scrolls.

literal: He had nine sons; Qinming was the most renowned.
idiomatic: He had nine sons; Qinming was best known.

literal: Shi's younger brother Yi, styled Wenruo, had fine bearing and discernment.
idiomatic: Shi's younger brother Yi, styled Wenruo, had grace and judgment.

literal: At eleven he married Emperor Wen's daughter the Princess of Pingyuan, was appointed Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and enfeoffed Duke of Anping.
idiomatic: At eleven he married Emperor Wen's daughter, Princess of Pingyuan, became Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant, and was enfeoffed Duke of Anping.

literal: In the sixteenth year of Datong he was advanced to commandery duke, made Grand Commander, and attended in Emperor Wen's tent guard, guarding within the palace at night.
idiomatic: In Datong year sixteen he was made commandery duke and Grand Commander, guarding Emperor Wen's tent by night.

literal: He was transferred to General of the Martial Guard.
idiomatic: He became General of the Martial Guard.

literal: When Jin pacified Jiangling, what he received from the grants of military goods he divided and gave to his sons.
idiomatic: When Jin took Jiangling, he divided the military spoils among his sons.

literal: Yi took nothing for himself; he only selected and rewarded by name youths of reputation within his household who had scholar's bearing, treating them separately.
idiomatic: Yi took nothing; he only singled out reputable youths of scholar's bearing in his household and favored them.

literal: When Emperor Wen heard of it he granted two hundred male and female slaves; Yi firmly declined and would not accept.
idiomatic: Emperor Wen heard and granted two hundred slaves; Yi firmly refused.

literal: Shortly he was appointed Grand General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Opening the Government with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: Soon he was Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry with Opening the Government's ceremonial rank.
